meta.description: CBT self-help exercises inspired by Feeling Good: the Negative Thought Journal, Negative Thought Counter, Daily Activity Plan, Anti-Procrastination Table, and the "But" Rebuttal. Write your thoughts down, see them clearly, and move a little lighter.

home.eyebrow: CBT exercises inspired by Feeling Good by Dr. David Burns
home.title:
Write it down.
Let it settle.
home.desc: Approach the tests and exercises with a still mind. You are gradually mastering ideas and techniques that have proven especially effective in helping you overcome painful emotions.
home.note: No judgment, no rush. Go at your own pace.

tools.heading: The Toolkit
tools.intro: Each tool mirrors an exercise from Feeling Good. Start with whatever feels easiest today.

thought_journal.name: Negative Thought Journal
thought_journal.description: Write down the situation and the automatic thought in three or six columns, name the distortion, and answer it with reason.

thought_counter.name: Negative Thought Counter
thought_counter.description: Just one number a day: how often negative thoughts showed up. A line across the days shows the change.

daily_activity_plan.name: Daily Activity Plan
daily_activity_plan.description: Plan your day across fourteen time slots, note what actually happened, then rate mastery and pleasure.

anti_procrastination_table.name: Anti-Procrastination Table
anti_procrastination_table.description: Break a task into small steps and compare predicted versus actual difficulty and satisfaction. The dread shrinks.

but_rebuttal_tool.name: The "But" Rebuttal
but_rebuttal_tool.description: For every "but …" excuse, write a more realistic, more rational rebuttal — until procrastination has nowhere to stand.
